newsitem.title: UK: Champagne celebrations could go phut, not pop.
newsitem.headline: Champagne celebrations could go phut, not pop.

text.p: Champagne celebrations could soon go with a phut not a pop.
People need no longer shrink with nervousness at parties if a revolutionary new cork catches on that takes the explosive fizz out of a bottle opening.
A tiny pull tab reduces the cork's width. A hole in the cap then releases gas from the neck of the bottle.

"Many of our clients are women and old folk who enjoy champagne but find the opening of a bottle a daunting experience," said Philippe Bienvenue, sales director for Cattier, one firm experimenting with the new cork.
Jacques Pitoux, an advertising salesman who invented the cork, acted when he lost a quarter of bottle one night in froth.

"With the current price of champagne, that was several pounds (dollars) worth gone for nothing. So I...designed a new cork," he told Thursday's New Scientist weekly. But traditionalists need not fear. Inventor Pitoux said: "If you want to pop the cork or even crack the bottle with a sabre, you simply don't pull the tab and it works just the same as an ordinary cork."
